title: The wire: forge types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

ForgeAction.description: A write or a read that an item's page offers (#4329, #4361): forge/comment, forge/label, forge/close (a close, a reopen or a transition; closeNotPlanned is a close with reason not_planned, where the forge has it, #4404), forge/merge (now, or with auto), forge/approve, forge/request-changes (#5857), forge/rerun, forge/log, forge/diff, forge/add-child, forge/blocked-by, forge/assign (#4403), forge/cancel-auto-merge and forge/ready (#4410), and on an issue forge/priority and forge/hold (#6091, #6092).

ForgeAddChildRequest.description: forge/add-child (#3271): add a child to an epic's plan: a new issue (title, with level story, task, spike or bug) or one that is there (issue: #12, owner/repo#12, its URL, or a Linear key such as ENG-4). A new child gets the level's label and the epic's feature: label. GitHub and Linear.

ForgeApproveRequest.description: forge/approve (#3130): approve a pull request at sha, the head commit its page shows (refused when the head moved).

ForgeAssignRequest.description: forge/assign (#4403): people to assign to an issue or a pull request, and people to take off it, by their login on the forge. At most 10 of each at once.

ForgeBlockedByRequest.description: forge/blocked-by (#3271): the issues that block a child of a plan, to add and to take off, by node. GitHub and Linear.

ForgeBoards.description: forge/boards (#3282): the boards of the projects of this machine's folders, each once, by url, in its project's order.

ForgeBoardsRequest.description: forge/boards (#3282): the boards of every folder's project on this machine, or of one folder's.

ForgeCapabilities.description: What one forge on a list's page fills (#4329, #4361), so a client hides what it does not: issues and pulls say it has them; labelColors that its labels have a #rrggbb colour; avatars that its items have authorAvatar; stateReason that its closed issues have stateReason. createdAt that its items have createdAt, and closedAt that its closed and merged items have closedAt; children, linkedPulls and events that an item's read has them (#4373); total that it counts a list's items, for ForgeList.total (#4396); releases that it has releases, for forge/releases and forge/release (#4426); a pull request's fields (#4409): branches that it has headRef and baseRef, mergedBy and mergeCommit that a merged one says them, size that its read has additions, deletions and commits, reviewers and closes that its read has them, and checkTimes that its checks have startedAt and finishedAt; priority and hold that forge/priority and forge/hold set an issue's priority and on hold, in the forge's own field or else by the labels (#6091); each is absent from an earlier daemon, which has none. commentCount says how to read ForgeItem.comments: exact; capped at commentsMost (show 50+ there); or detail, only on an item's own page (hide it on the row).

ForgeChanges.description: forge/changes (#6349, epic #6348): a page of the items that changed at or after the request's updatedSince, each a whole ForgeItem with its updatedAt, newest first within each source. nextPageCursor is the next page, absent at the end. highWater is the latest updatedAt of the read so far, carried from page to page, so the last page's is the read's: a client keeps it as its cursor for the next read (and asks from a minute before it). While a source in the read could not be read (errors), highWater does not move past updatedSince, so the next read asks again from there; with no item, highWater is updatedSince (0 for none), so a client keeps the later of it and its cursor. errors says a source that could not be read, and the items of the others still come; forges says what each forge on the page fills, as ForgeList's does.

ForgeChangesRequest.description: forge/changes (#6349): the issues and pull requests of one source (a ForgeSource's source; every source on this machine when not said) that changed at or after updatedSince, in every state (open, closed and merged); every item when not said, for a first fill. kinds is issue, pr or both. limit is 1 to 100, 100 when not said; pageCursor is the last page's nextPageCursor, with the same source, kinds and updatedSince.

ForgeCheck.description: One of a pull request's checks (#3129): a check run or a commit status. state is passing, failing, running or skipped; url is its page on the forge. startedAt and finishedAt are when it started and ended (#4409), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities.checkTimes): absent on a check that has not started, and finishedAt on one still running; a commit status has neither.

ForgeChecks.description: forge/checks (#6349): the checks summary of each pull request asked for that the forge still has, in one call on GitHub; on another forge from its list of open pull requests, so one that is no longer open is left out. at is when they were read. A pull request's checks do not move its updatedAt, so a changed-since read does not see them.

ForgeChecksRequest.description: forge/checks (#6349): the pull requests of one source (a ForgeSource's source), by their numbers, 1 to 100 of them.

ForgeChecksRow.description: One pull request's checks summary (#6349), in ForgeItem's words: state is open, closed or merged; checks is passing, failing, running or none; review is approved, changes_requested or review_required; mergeable is mergeable, conflicting or unknown; autoMerge says auto-merge is on. Each is absent where the forge does not say it.

ForgeCloseReason.description: Why forge/close closes an issue (#4404): completed, or not_planned where the forge has it (the action closeNotPlanned).

ForgeCloseRequest.description: forge/close (#3130): close an issue or a pull request, or with reopen open it again; with transition, move a Jira issue by that transition of its workflow, by its id from the page's transitions (#3260). reason is why an issue closes (#4404): completed (the default) or not_planned, which only an issue whose actions have closeNotPlanned takes; refused with reopen or a transition, and on a pull request.

ForgeComment.description: A comment on an issue or a pull request (#3129), as Markdown. bot says a bot or an app wrote it. avatar is the author's picture, a URL that only forge/image reads (#4363); none when the forge gives none.

ForgeCommentCount.description: How a forge counts an item's comments (#4329): exact; capped at the forge's commentsMost (Linear's 50); or detail, only on an item's own page (Bitbucket issues, Azure Repos), so a list's count is 0.

ForgeCommentRequest.description: forge/comment (#3130): a comment, as Markdown, on an issue or a pull request, as the person whose machine it is.

ForgeDiff.description: forge/diff (#3130): a pull request's changed files at its head, as the app's own diff draws them (#1341); cut says some files are listed with no hunks; url is its files on the forge.

ForgeDiffFile.description: One file a pull request changes (#3130): change is added, removed, modified or renamed; note says why it has no hunks, when it has none.

ForgeDiffHunk.description: One @@ block of a file's diff (#3130).

ForgeDone.description: What a forge write did (#3130): url is the comment or the item on the forge; auto says a merge waits for the checks; reran is how many runs or pipelines were run again. item is the item the write was on, as the forge has it after the write, with its updatedAt (#6351, epic #6348): a client cache replaces its optimistic value with it. On forge/add-child it is the epic. Absent when the read after the write failed (the write still happened), and from an earlier daemon.

ForgeEvent.description: One event on an issue's timeline (#4373), as its forge says it: kind is what happened; actor is who did it, absent when the forge says nobody (a deleted account); label is the label that labelled and unlabelled name; assignee is the person that assigned and unassigned name; source is the issue or pull request that referenced names, or the pull request that closed closed it with.

ForgeEventKind.description: What happened on an issue (#4373): a label was added or removed, a person assigned or unassigned, it closed or reopened, or another issue or pull request named it.

ForgeHoldRequest.description: forge/hold (#6091): put an issue on hold (on) or take it off hold. The daemon writes the forge's own field where it has one (Bitbucket: the state on hold; Jira: a status named On hold where the workflow has one), else the label on hold.

ForgeIds.description: forge/ids (#6349): a page of the nodes of the items the source has now in the states asked, at most 1,000 a page. nextPageCursor is the next page, absent at the end. A client removes from its cache an item of those kinds and states that no page named: it was deleted, moved, or the person can no longer see it. A read that fails is an error, never a short list. at is when the read began (the first page's time, on every page): an item that changed after it can be missing from the pages, so a client keeps a cached item whose updatedAt is at or after at.

ForgeIdsRequest.description: forge/ids (#6349): the ids of one source's items (a ForgeSource's source) of kinds (issue, pr or both) in states: open, closed (a closed pull request includes a merged one), or both when not said. pageCursor is the last page's nextPageCursor, with the same source, kinds and states.

ForgeImage.description: forge/image (#4009): an image's bytes, so that a client never loads a forge page's remote URL. mimeType is image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp, read from the bytes. keep false (#7138): the read went through a host that the person allowed or showed, so a client does not put it on disk; absent, only a forge's own image hosts.

ForgeImageRequest.description: forge/image (#4009): the url of an image on a forge page. Only a forge's own image hosts (for GitHub: github.com's user-attachments and repo assets, and user-images, private-user-images, raw and avatars on githubusercontent.com), the hosts that the person allowed (imageHosts/list) and those in show are read; another host is the failure imageBlocked, with ImageBlocked as its data. show (#7138) is the exact hosts that the person accepts for this one read, at most 6, from the person's own clients only. The forge's token goes only to its own hosts, and to none after a hop through a host that the person chose.

ForgeItem.description: An issue or a pull request (a GitLab merge request) as its forge says it (#3129): one model for GitHub, GitLab, Linear and Jira (#3260), so one page draws each. node is its lineage node (kind issue or pr, ref github:issue:alexec/agents#12). state is open, closed or merged; status is the tracker's own name for its step, where its workflow has steps (a Jira status, as In Progress; one in Jira's Done category is closed). folder is a folder on this machine on its repo, to act from. labels have their #rrggbb colour where the forge gives one (#2956). The pull request's own fields: draft; checks is passing, failing, running or none; review is approved, changes_requested or review_required; mergeable is mergeable, conflicting or unknown; autoMerge says auto-merge is on. The hierarchy (#3267): parent is the issue it is a sub-issue (a Linear or GitLab child) of; level is epic, story, task or spike, from its labels; feature is the name of its feature:<name> label; progress is a parent's closed children of all of them, where the forge says it: in a GitHub list, and on an issue's own read. standing says it has the label standing: a standing epic, whose plan is a query (#3659). authorAvatar is the author's picture, a URL that only forge/image reads (#4363), where the forge gives one (ForgeCapabilities.avatars). stateReason is why a closed issue closed (#4365): completed, not_planned or duplicate, where the forge says it (ForgeCapabilities.stateReason); absent on an open issue and on a pull request. createdAt is when it opened and closedAt when it closed or merged (#4373), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities.createdAt and closedAt); closedAt is absent while it is open. A pull request's branches (#4409): headRef is the branch it merges from and baseRef the one it merges into, where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities.branches); on its own read at least, and on a list's row where the list says them. A merged pull request's mergedBy is who merged it and mergeCommit the commit it made on baseRef (ForgeCapabilities.mergedBy and mergeCommit); each is absent while it is open or closed unmerged. priority is high, medium or low, absent for none (#5688, #5747): from the forge's own priority field where it has one, and then its labels are not read for it: Linear's (Urgent and High → high; Low → low), Jira's (Highest and High → high; Low and Lowest → low), GitHub's Priority issue field when the repo has it (Urgent and High → high), Bitbucket's (blocker and critical → high; major, the default, → none; minor and trivial → low) and Azure DevOps' Priority (1 → high; 2, the default, → none; 3 and 4 → low); elsewhere from the labels priority:high, priority:medium and priority:low (any case; the higher of two). milestoneDue is the due date of the item's milestone, where the forge says it; absent with no milestone or no due date. onHold says the item is on hold (#5747): Bitbucket's state on hold; elsewhere the label on hold (any case; on-hold too), and on Jira a status named On hold too; absent is false.

ForgeItemDetail.description: forge/issue and forge/pull (#3129): one item with its body (Markdown) and a page of its comments, the newest page first and at most 50, oldest first in the page; cursor is the page before it, absent at the first comment. A pull request's checks, review threads (line comments, in threads) and files changed come with it. head is a pull request's head commit, which forge/merge and forge/approve name (#3130); mergeMethods are the ways its repo allows, the repo's default first; start is the new-agent form for an issue. transitions are the moves an issue's workflow allows now (Jira, #3260), which forge/close takes in place of a close or a reopen. actions are what the item's page offers now, from its forge and its state (#4361): a merged pull request has no merge and no reopen, a closed item no close; absent from an earlier daemon, when the page shows what it did before. On an issue's read (#4373), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities): children are its sub-issues, linkedPulls the pull requests that close it, and events its timeline, oldest first (labelled, assigned, closed, referenced and the like); each is absent where the forge gives none. On a pull request's read (#4409), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities): additions, deletions and commits are its size; reviewers are the people asked to review it and the people who reviewed it, each once with their newest state; closes are the issues it closes when it merges. viewer is the login this machine reads and writes the forge as (#5804), the one forge/approve reviews as, so a client knows which reviewer and which author is the person; absent where the connection does not say it, and from an earlier daemon.

ForgeItemRequest.description: forge/issue and forge/pull (#3129): the item's lineage node, and for an older page of its comments the cursor of the page after it.

ForgeLabel.description: A label on an issue or a pull request (#3129), with its #rrggbb colour where the forge gives one (#2956).

ForgeLabelRequest.description: forge/label (#3130): labels to add to an issue or a pull request, and labels to take off it, by name.

ForgeLabels.description: forge/labels (#3130): the labels an issue or a pull request can have, at most 100, by name.

ForgeLead.description: An epic's lead session (#3267): its id, title and state.

ForgeLinked.description: An item that an issue's read names (#4373): a sub-issue, or a pull request that closes it; or an issue that a pull request closes (#4409). state is open, closed or merged, as ForgeItem.state.

ForgeList.description: forge/issues and forge/pulls (#3129): a page of items, the last updated first. cursor is the next page, absent at the end. errors says a forge that could not be read (not connected, a rate limit), and the items of the others still come. forges says what each forge on the page fills (#4361); absent from an earlier daemon. total is how many items the whole list has, the sum of each forge's count, kept from each forge's first page (#4396); absent when a forge on the list gives no count (ForgeCapabilities.total) or could not be read, and from an earlier daemon. scopes says what the list reads (#6641).

readAt.description: When the forges were read for this answer (#6642): an answer agentsd kept has the time of its read, not of the call. Absent from an earlier daemon.

scopes.description: What the list reads (#6641): one entry per repo or project, as forge:name (github:example/shop), or one per forge that names no repos. Two machines whose lists read the same scopes give the same list, so a client asks one of them. Absent from an earlier daemon.

ForgeListError.description: A forge forge/issues or forge/pulls could not read (#3129): forge is github, gitlab or linear.

ForgeListRequest.description: forge/issues and forge/pulls (#3129): the issues or pull requests of every folder on this machine, or of one folder's repo. state is open (when not said), closed or all; a closed pull request includes a merged one. label, assignee (a login) and query (words in the title or body) narrow the list. limit is 1 to 100, 50 when not said; cursor is the last page's. feature (a name: work for the label feature:work) narrows it to one feature's items (#3267). board (a board's url, from forge/boards) narrows it to one board's items (#3282). updatedSince narrows it to the items that changed at or after that time (#6349); an earlier daemon leaves it out and lists every item.

sort.description: The order (#6538): priority (High, then Medium, then Low, then none, each newest first; GitHub by the priority labels, Jira by its priority field), else the last updated first. A forge that cannot sort by priority (GitLab) lists the last updated first; an older daemon too.

fresh.description: true reads the forges, not the answer agentsd keeps for a minute (#6642): a Refresh. An earlier daemon leaves it out and can answer from its copy.

ForgeLog.description: forge/log (#3130): the last lines of each failed check's log, as plain text.

ForgeLogRequest.description: forge/log (#3130): the end of a pull request's failed checks' logs, or of one check by name.

ForgeLogins.description: people/setForgeLogins (#2951): the caller's own GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira (#3313), Forgejo (#3836), Bitbucket and Azure DevOps (#3853) logins, for Settings ▸ You, replacing what was kept; blank clears one.

ForgeMergeMethod.description: How forge/merge merges a pull request (#3130): a merge commit, one squashed commit, or its commits rebased onto the base.

ForgeMergeRequest.description: forge/merge (#3130): merge a pull request at sha, the head commit its page shows (refused when the head moved), by method (the repo's default when absent); with auto, the forge merges it once its checks pass.

ForgeNext.description: forge/next (#5689): the work that is ready, in one order, at most 100 rows. The top row that is not on hold is the next one to pick up. readAt is when this answer was made; the forge reads in it may be up to the forge cache's minute older. errors says a forge that could not be read, as ForgeList's does; the rows of the others still come.

ForgeNextRequest.description: forge/next (#5689): the folder whose work is read. epic (an issue's lineage node) gives only that epic's children, or a standing epic's query (#3661). level epic gives the open epics instead of the issues, in the same order, to choose which epic gets a lead; it takes no epic.

ForgeNextRow.description: A row of forge/next (#5689): an item that is ready (open, not an epic unless the level is epic, no open blocked by, and not taken: no session on this machine that is not archived is labelled with it, no open pull request fixes it, and it has no assignee), or one that is on hold and otherwise ready. place is its place, 1 first. The order: not on hold first; then priority high, medium, none, low; then the milestone's due date, the earliest first, no due date last; then the oldest (createdAt, then the lowest number). reasons are short words for the keys that put it there, as priority high, milestone Work, due 20 Nov, and oldest (when its age put it above the next row). onHold says it is on hold: it is never the next one, and its first reason is on hold.

ForgeNodeRequest.description: forge/labels, forge/rerun and forge/diff (#3130): the issue or pull request.

ForgePlan.description: forge/plan (#3267): an epic and its plan. children are its sub-issues (at most 100), step by step, in the forge's order within a step. steps are the children of each step, the first first. lead is the session on this machine, not archived, that works on the epic in lineage (its label #<n>, or the Linear key) and is labelled lead. standing is set only for a standing epic (#3661): its children are then the open issues of its query, not its sub-issues, at most 100, in the order of forge/next (#5689: not on hold first, then priority, the milestone's due date and the oldest), all in one step 1; its item has no progress.

ForgePlanChild.description: A child of an epic in forge/plan (#3267). blockedBy are the issues it is blocked by, open or closed, in the plan or not. step is 1 for a child that no other child blocks, else one more than the last step of the children that block it; a blocker outside the plan adds no step, and children in a loop share the step after the rest. blockedOutside are its open blockers outside the plan (an issue of another epic). A forge with no dependencies (GitLab Free) puts every child in step 1.

ForgePlanRequest.description: forge/plan (#3267): the epic's lineage node, an issue on GitHub, GitLab or Linear.

ForgePlanStep.description: A step of a plan (#3267): its number, from 1, and its children's nodes.

ForgePriorityRequest.description: forge/priority (#6091): set an issue's priority to high, medium or low, or to none when priority is absent. The daemon writes the forge's own field where it has one (#5747: Linear, Jira, GitHub's Priority issue field, Bitbucket, Azure Boards), else the label priority:<priority>, and takes off the other two.

ForgeProgress.description: A parent issue's children (#3267): done are closed, of total.

ForgeRelease.description: A release on a forge (#4426). node is its lineage node (kind release, ref <forge>:<repo>/release/<tag>), which forge/release reads and lineage keys its cost by. repo is the repo as the forge names it, and folder a folder on it. latest is the repo's newest published release that is neither a draft nor a pre-release. publishedAt is absent on a draft; author and authorAvatar when the forge says them; assets is how many files it has.

ForgeReleaseDetail.description: forge/release (#4426): a release, the release before it (previous, its tag; absent for the first), how many commits are between the two (commits, at most what the forge's compare gives) and the pull requests they merged, from each squash commit's (#n) or (!n), oldest first. compareUrl is the forge's page of the range.

ForgeReleasePull.description: A pull request in a release (#4426): its node, its number, and its title as its squash commit says it, with the (#n) taken off; sha is the commit.

ForgeReleaseRequest.description: forge/release (#4426): a release's lineage node, as ForgeRelease.node says it.

ForgeReleases.description: forge/releases (#4426): the releases of the folders' repos, newest first (a draft, which has no publishedAt, by createdAt). none are the forges in reach that have no releases, and why, so a client says so (Linear and Jira have no releases); errors are the forges that could not be read.

ForgeReleasesRequest.description: forge/releases (#4426): the releases of every folder's repo on this machine, or of one folder's, at most limit (1 to 100, 30 when absent) of each repo.

ForgeRequestChangesRequest.description: forge/request-changes (#5857): request changes on a pull request at sha, the head commit its page shows (refused when the head moved). body is the review text, and it is required.

ForgeReviewer.description: A reviewer of a pull request (#4409): login is who; avatar their picture, a URL that only forge/image reads, where the forge gives one; state is their newest review, or pending while they are asked and have not answered, or were asked again since.

ForgeReviewerState.description: A reviewer's state (#4409): approved, changes_requested, commented (reviewed with no verdict) or pending (asked, not answered).

ForgeSource.description: A forge source this machine reads (#6349): source is the forge's name and the repository, project or team in lower case, as its nodes' refs name it (github:agentloops-dev/agent-loops, gitlab:group/project, jira:proj, linear:eng; linear for a whole Linear workspace), the key of a client cache's records. kinds is what it has: issue, pr or both. folder is a folder on this machine on it.

ForgeSources.description: forge/sources (#6349): the forge sources this machine reads, from its folders, so a client asks one machine for each source, not every machine. errors says a forge whose sources could not all be found (not connected).

ForgeStanding.description: A standing epic's query (#3659, #3661), as the daemon read it from the standing block in the epic's body. labels: the issue has all of them; any: at least one of them; not: none of them; milestone: none, any or a milestone's name; parent: none, only issues that are no other issue's sub-issue (#4335, #4348). lanes is how many lanes its lead runs at once, 1 when the block does not say. error says why there is no query: no block, a second block, or an unknown or bad field; with an error, the plan has no children.

ForgeStart.description: The new-agent form for an issue (#3130, Start Agent), as a view's agents/start-agent fills it (#834): the prompt, the session's labels, and a new worktree's name.

ForgeTransition.description: A move an issue's workflow allows now (#3260): its id, which forge/close takes, and its name, as Start Progress. category is the status category it goes to: new, indeterminate or done.

ImageBlocked.description: The data of the failure imageBlocked of forge/image (#7138): host is the host that was refused, exact and in ASCII; from is the host that redirected to it, absent when it is the image's own.

ImageHost.description: A host that the person allowed forge/image to read images from on one machine (#7138): the exact host, lower case and in ASCII, and when.

ImageHosts.description: imageHosts/list, and the list after imageHosts/allow and imageHosts/remove (#7138): at most 100 hosts, the first allowed first. The forges' own image hosts are not in it.

ProviderForget.description: providers/forget (#3398): the provider was removed; its machine ends its server and deletes its secrets.

RequestForge.description: The forge item a request is (spec 3862 §4).

label.description: alex-todo or needs-account on an issue; review-requested on a pull request with a review requested from the person (#5803), which is no label.

checklist.description: An issue's lines under its first "## What <name> does" heading.

screenshots.description: A pull request's image links under its "## Screenshots" heading.

updatedAt.description: The item's, when it was last read: a newer one is read again.

seenAt.description: The last sweep that saw it open with the label.

ReviewDismissRequest.description: reviews/dismiss (#3330): a person's Dismiss on a pull request in the sidebar's For Review. The host keeps it, so that pull request is not listed again.

url.description: The pull request's page, as its ReviewPull says it.

ReviewOpenRequest.description: reviews/open (#3464): a person opened a pull request's page from the sidebar's For Review. The host keeps it, so its row is drawn read on every client.

url.description: The pull request's page, as its ReviewPull says it.

ReviewPull.description: An open pull request with a review requested from the person (#5803), a UI change waiting for them (#2811), in the sidebar's For Review (#3330) until they review it, it is closed, or it is dismissed.

ref.description: Its lineage ref, "github:owner/name#12" or "gitlab:group/project!12": a press opens its Work page in the app. Nil from an older host: a press opens its forge page.

opened.description: The person has opened its page (reviews/open, #3464): its row is drawn read, not bold.
